acip: [D24] NGAG DON NI SHES BYA CHOS CAN, BYANG CHUB SEMS DPAS MTHAR SHES BYA'I SGRIB PA MA LUS PAR SPANGS PAR 'THOB NUS TE, DES CHOS THAMS CAD BDEN MED DU RIGS PAS GTAM LA PHAB CING, SGOM BYUNG GIS NYAMS SU BLANGS PAS 'PHAGS LAM RNAM PAR MI RTOG PA'I YE SHES RIM CAN DU SKYES TE BDEN 'DZIN GYI SA BON MA LUS PAR SPONG NUS PA'I PHYIR,
wylie: [d24] ngag don ni shes bya chos can, byang chub sems dpas mthar shes bya'i sgrib pa ma lus par spangs par 'thob nus te, des chos thams cad bden med du rigs pas gtam la phab cing, sgom byung gis nyams su blangs pas 'phags lam rnam par mi rtog pa'i ye shes rim can du skyes te bden 'dzin gyi sa bon ma lus par spong nus pa'i phyir
english: And then the following syllogism expresses what's being stated here: Consider each and every knowable thing in the universe. The bodhisattva is indeed able, in the end, to rid themselves of each and every obstacle to the state of omniscience; Because they first learn the logical conversation which allows them to establish that nothing in the universe is real; and then through their formal meditation practice they gradually make this understanding into a personal, meditational realization: they develop, step by step, the path of the realized ones—the wisdom which no longer imagines that things are real. [Incidentally, Kedrup Je then goes on in his text to demonstrate how these four levels of deep practice are problematic in the lower schools which still assert that the functionality of things is innate to them—a group of schools which includes the present, Mind Only School!] Appendix E: Eight arguments on the existence of foundation consciousness There are eight famous arguments used to support the belief of the Mind Only School that a foundation consciousness does indeed exist.  They are presented by Je Tsongkapa in both the root text and autocommentary of his Difficult Points in the Mind Only School, and thus commented upon by The Blade in his Golden Key. We have added the Key to this translation project precisely because it does make it easier for all of us to then make the deep jump into Je Tsongkapa's much more difficult treatment.
